source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026, USPSTF. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.

incidence.rank_among_cancers: ~1.0% of new cancer cases; relatively rare but disproportionately lethal
incidence.trend: Incidence declining ~1%/yr; mortality falling faster (~2.7%/yr), reflecting earlier-stage shift and survival gains

mortality.us_annual_deaths: ~12,450 projected for 2026 — the 14th leading cause of cancer death; deadliest gynecologic cancer
mortality.trend: ~49% diagnosed at distant stage (down from ~57% a decade earlier); survival rises sharply with earlier detection but no effective general-population screening exists

risk_factors.detail: Major hereditary risk; also predicts PARP-inhibitor benefit
MMR-deficiency syndromes raise risk (esp. endometrioid/clear cell)
Most diagnosed at 55-64; nulliparity, early menarche/late menopause
Associated with clear cell and endometrioid histotypes
Parity, breastfeeding, oral contraceptive use, tubal ligation/salpingectomy reduce risk

screening.guideline_summary: USPSTF recommends AGAINST screening average-risk asymptomatic women (CA-125/transvaginal ultrasound do not reduce mortality and cause harm). High-risk (e.g., BRCA) management is individualized, including risk-reducing surgery. Cite USPSTF; NCCN not used.
screening.notes: Absence of effective screening is central to the late-stage-diagnosis problem; many high-grade serous cancers arise from the fallopian tube (STIC)

epidemiology.presentation: Often vague and late: bloating, pelvic/abdominal pain, early satiety, urinary urgency; frequently advanced at diagnosis
